text:
maria: Quick question — when a route has both a host capture (eg `*.{team}.example.com`) and a path wildcard with captures (`/v1/:resource/*`), what's our canonical precedence? I'm seeing surprising matches in staging.

devin: We currently evaluate host then path then headers. But ordering within host patterns (exact vs capture vs wildcard) wasn't well-specified — that bite us.

tanay: +1. My proposal: exact host > host-capture (named) > host-wildcard. For paths: exact > param captures (named) > single-segment wildcard `*` > catch-all `**`. That matches intuition and minimizes surprise.

louise: That seems reasonable. Edge case: multiple captures with same specificity, which service wins? We need deterministic tiebreaker (creation timestamp or explicit weight).

maria: I prefer explicit weight on the route config rather than opaque creation-time rules. Console can show a small warning when weight is used.

devin: Agreed. Additions: header anchors (explicit header matches) should outrank captures, because header-based routing is narrower control from product teams. So final order: host exact > host-capture > host-wildcard; then header anchors, then path rules specificity as tanay described; then service weight.

raj: Quick example for clarity:
```
- host: api.eu.example.com -> svc-v2
- host: *.eu.example.com (capture team) -> svc-team
- host: *.example.com (wildcard) -> svc-global
- header: x-tenant=vip -> svc-vip
- path: /v1/payments/:id -> svc-pay
- path: /v1/* -> svc-v1
```
Request to `payments.eu.example.com` with `x-tenant=vip` and path `/v1/payments/123` should route to `svc-vip` (header outranks host-capture). Without header it goes to `svc-team` (host-capture outranks host-wildcard).

devin: Exactly. Also we should add a deterministic explain plan in the console and API: `GET /explain?host=...&path=...` -> returns the winning rule id and a short trace of the comparisons. That helps oncall and users.

maria: Can we include a small text hint in the route edit UI: "This route will be evaluated after host-level anchors. Use weight only for controlled failovers".

louise: Telemetry: emit a metric `route.match.reason` with labels {selected_rule, candidate_rules, tie_breaker, explain_version}. That will let us detect frequent collisions.

tanay: Also prefer conservative fallbacks on capacity-constrained zones: if a match's model (dedicated vs hosted) isn't available, fallback to compatible model variant but keep match reason and fallback reason in the explain output. For routes that rely on service weight, ensure fallback respects weight order.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: route-matcher-spec v3 -> staging (canary=10%).

maria: I'll review the spec PR. One more UX ask: console should surface "why this route lost" inline (hover over losing route) — not just the winner. Very helpful for self-serve teams. :eyes:

devin: Good call. We'll also add a linter in `redwoodctl validate routes` to flag ambiguous overlapping host+path combos and suggest anchor hints.

raj: I'll prototype an `explain` CLI response sample for docs. Example output idea:
```
selected: route-432
reasons:
  - host: matched by capture '*.eu.example.com' (priority 2)
  - header: x-tenant not present (required by higher priority rule)
  - path: '/v1/payments/123' matched '/v1/:resource' (priority 3)
fallbacks: []
```

maria: Perfect. If we can get spec + console mock + linter in next week, I'll schedule a customer-facing note for teams about updated precedence semantics.

louise: Filed a ticket for telemetry + UI hints: INF-2419.

devin: Thanks all — I'll update the RFC to include explicit numeric priorities and the explain API contract.
